STRATEGY BRAIN (team O)

Board: cells 0-15, rows of 4. Lines to check: 4 rows, 4 columns, 2 diagonals (10 lines total). Each 4-cell line is a threat when it holds 3 of one side and 1 empty cell.

Move priority each turn (captain checks in this order):

2. Block: if any line has 3 of theirs + 1 empty, play that empty cell (unless step 1 applies).
3. Double-threat check for opponent: list every empty cell where they would make two open 3-lines at once. If one exists, occupy it or make a forcing threat that lands on it.
4. Create our own double threat: find an empty cell that gives us two open 3-lines (each with empty 4th cell) so they can only block one.
5. Otherwise take a free cell from the 4 centers (5,6,9,10) or 4 corners (0,3,12,15). They lie on 3 lines each. Avoid edge cells (1,2,4,7,8,11,13,14) early; they lie on only 2 lines.

args.text:
Team X strategy (4x4 tic-tac-toe, 4 in a row wins, cells 0-15 row by row).

1) Each move, check in order: (a) can we win now? (b) must we block an opponent 4-line that has 3 of theirs and 1 empty, including broken shapes like X X _ X? (c) can we make a fork, i.e. one move creating two open threats at once?
2) If no immediate win/block, prefer centre cells 5, 6, 9, 10: they lie on the most 4-lines (row, column, diagonal, and more). Corners lie on the fewest; use them mainly to block or to finish.
3) Before each move, list every 4-line through the candidate cell, for us and for them. Count threats, not just cells.
4) Watch for opponent forks: if they have a move that would create two threats, block the shared cell or create our own forcing threat first.
5) Forcing play: a threat that must be answered gives us tempo; use it to set up a fork.
6) Captain proposes one cell with a one-line reason naming the threat or fork it addresses. Voters check: missed win, missed block, missed opponent fork. Vote false if any is missed.
7) Retro: note which opening and which replies worked or failed, and which opponent patterns recurred. Keep this brain short and rule-based.
